title: The Perturbation Forge
topics: degenerate perturbation theory and good quantum numbers
p^4 and p^6 corrections of the oscillator

sources.where: Ch. 11.1-11.2 (pp. 114-123): time-independent perturbation theory, Stark effect
Q1 anharmonic oscillator, Q2 Stark effect

intro: The forge heats a level and bends it: $H=H_0+\lambda H'$. Perturbation theory is a recurring exam topic (FS19, HS18, FS22, FS26, HS25, HS21), always in the same three flavours: non-degenerate (energies and states order by order), degenerate (diagonalise $H'$ inside the degenerate subspace, use symmetries), and the hydrogen corrections where the trick is to eliminate $p^2$ with the Schroedinger equation. The shortcut for everything: find which matrix elements $\langle m|H'|n\rangle$ vanish.

tutorial.title: The anvil
tutorial.html: The two dashed lines are the unperturbed levels $\varepsilon_{1,2}=\mp\Delta/2$ crossing at $\Delta=0$. The solid curves are the exact eigenvalues once a coupling $V$ is switched on: the levels repel and never cross (avoided crossing).

tutorial.title: The glowing markers
tutorial.html: The orange marker is the exact lower level, the green marker is second-order perturbation theory $\varepsilon_1-V^2/\Delta$. They agree for $|\Delta|\gg V$ and separate when $|\Delta|\lesssim 2V$: this is exactly where the condition $|H'_{mn}|\ll|E_n-E_m|$ fails and you must switch to degenerate theory.

tutorial.title: Consoles
tutorial.html: Library: the four exam recipes. Quiz: multiple choice. Derivation desk: the proofs the exams ask for (FS19 Q4(i) is 10 points of pure derivation). Fights: Stark effect, linear perturbation, time-dependent transition probability. Boss gate: FS19/HS18 Q4, FS26 Q4, FS22 Q4.

encounters.title: Non-degenerate perturbation theory: E1, E2 and the corrected state

blocks.html: Write $H=H_0+\lambda H'$ with $H_0\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$ solved and non-degenerate. Make the power-series ansatz $\psi=\psi_n+\lambda\psi^{(1)}+\lambda^2\psi^{(2)}+\dots$, $E=E_n+\lambda E^{(1)}+\lambda^2E^{(2)}+\dots$ and fix the normalisation convention $\langle\psi_n|\psi^{(s)}\rangle=0$ for $s\ge1$ (the exam asks you to state it). Insert into $H\psi=E\psi$ and compare powers of $\lambda$:

blocks.label: every order has the same operator H_0 - E_n on the left

blocks.html: Project on $\langle\psi_n|$: the left-hand side vanishes because $H_0$ is hermitian ($\langle\psi_n|(H_0-E_n)=0$). This leaves the energies. Project on $\langle\psi_m|$, $m\ne n$: $(E_m-E_n)\langle\psi_m|\psi^{(1)}\rangle=-\langle\psi_m|H'|\psi_n\rangle$ gives the state. Here is where non-degeneracy is needed: you divide by $E_m-E_n$.

blocks.tex: E^{(1)}_n=\langle n|H'|n\rangle,\qquad E^{(2)}_n=\sum_{m\neq n}\frac{|\langle m|H'|n\rangle|^2}{E_n-E_m},\qquad \psi^{(1)}_n=\sum_{m\neq n}\frac{\langle m|H'|n\rangle}{E_n-E_m}\,\psi_m
blocks.label: script Ch. 11.1; given on the HS25 Q3 sheet

blocks.html: Level repulsion. A state with a neighbour $m$ above ($E_m>E_n$) is pushed down, a neighbour below pushes it up. For the ground state $E^{(2)}_0\le0$ always, since every denominator is negative. The two-level case $H=\begin{pmatrix}\varepsilon_1&V\\V&\varepsilon_2\end{pmatrix}$ has exact levels $\frac{\varepsilon_1+\varepsilon_2}2\pm\frac12\sqrt{\Delta^2+4V^2}$, $\Delta=\varepsilon_2-\varepsilon_1$, and for $|\Delta|\gg V$ the lower one is $\varepsilon_1-V^2/\Delta$: exactly the second-order formula.

(1) The sum excludes $m=n$. (2) The denominator is $E_n-E_m$, not $E_m-E_n$: sign errors here flip the sign of $E^{(2)}$. (3) $E^{(2)}$ needs all couplings: in the oscillator, $x^4$ couples $n$ to $n\pm2$ and $n\pm4$, and you must list both directions ($n-2$ exists only for $n\ge2$). (4) The expansion is valid only if $|\langle m|\lambda H'|n\rangle|\ll|E_n-E_m|$. If two levels become close, use the degenerate method.

blocks.label: FS19 Q4(ii): only three states are coupled to the ground state

blocks.html: FS19 Q4 / HS18 Q4 (21 pt): (i) set up the series, state the convention, explain $\psi^{(1)}$ and $E^{(2)}$ (10 pt); (ii) work out the $p^4$ correction of the oscillator ground state to second order (7 pt); (iii) say how the $p^6$ term changes it (4 pt). HS25 Q3 gives the three formulas above and asks for the $a^2+a^{\dagger2}$ perturbation; FS22 Q4(i) is the same derivation with the degenerate twist.

encounters.title: Degenerate perturbation theory, symmetries and the Stark effect

blocks.html: If $E_m$ is $g$-fold degenerate the non-degenerate formula divides by zero: the unperturbed states $|i\rangle$ are not determined, $H'$ decides which combinations are the right zeroth-order states. In the project on the degenerate subspace the order-$\lambda$ equation becomes an eigenvalue problem (FS22 Q4(ii), 4 pt):

Do not diagonalise blindly: use symmetry. If an operator $A$ commutes with $H_0$ and $H'$ and the degenerate states have different $A$-eigenvalues, then $\langle i|H'|j\rangle=0$ for them (since $[A,H']=0$) and $W$ is already diagonal. For hydrogen with a central perturbation, $A=L^2,L_z$ makes the first-order shift simply $\langle nlm|H'|nlm\rangle$ (FS26 Q4(ii)).

blocks.tex: H_0=\hbar\omega\big(a^\dagger a+b^\dagger b+c^\dagger c+\tfrac32\big),\ \ H'=\omega L_z,\ \ L_z=i\hbar\,(ab^\dagger-a^\dagger b)\ \Rightarrow\ E^{(1)}\in\{+\hbar\omega,\,0,\,-\hbar\omega\}\ \text{on }E=\tfrac52\hbar\omega
blocks.label: FS22 Q4(iii): basis |100>, |010>, |001>

blocks.html: The three-fold level $\frac52\hbar\omega$ is the $l=1$ multiplet (vectors $x,y,z$): any rotation-invariant perturbation leaves it degenerate, and $L_z$ splits it into $m=+1,0,-1$. That is the SO(3) comment asked in FS22 Q4(iv).

Stark effect, $n=2$. $\Delta H=-e\vec E\cdot\vec x=-eEz$ with $e<0$. Four degenerate states $|2,l,m\rangle$. The operator $z$ commutes with $L_z$ ($\Delta m=0$) and is odd under parity ($\Delta l=\pm1$). Only $\langle200|z|210\rangle=-3a_0$ survives:

The Stark shift of $n=2$ is linear in $E$ because the states $2s$ and $2p$ are degenerate and have opposite parity (a permanent dipole $3ea_0$). For $n=1$ (non-degenerate, $\langle z\rangle=0$) the shift is quadratic. Do not diagonalise the $4\times4$ matrix with 16 entries when 14 of them are zero by selection rules.

check.q: In degenerate PT, the first-order energies are
options: the eigenvalues of $\langle i|H'|j\rangle$ restricted to the degenerate subspace
the eigenvalues of $H_0+H'$ in the full space
check.explain: Script (11.2.2): the order-$\lambda$ equation projected on the subspace is a $g\times g$ eigenvalue equation.

check.q: Why do $|2,1,\pm1\rangle$ show no linear Stark shift?
options: Because $\vec E$ is parallel to $z$, not to $x$ and $y$
$\langle 2,l',m'|z|2,1,\pm1\rangle=0$ for all $l',m'$ in the subspace: $z$ keeps $m$, and the only $m=\pm1$ states are the $2p$ states themselves with equal parity
check.explain: $z$ is odd and $\Delta m=0$: the only non-zero element in the $n=2$ subspace is $\langle200|z|210\rangle$.

encounters.title: Hydrogen fine structure: the relativistic kinetic correction

blocks.html: Typical electron speed in hydrogen is $v/c\approx0.007$, so relativity is a small correction. Expand the relativistic kinetic energy:

blocks.label: FS26 Q4(i); the p^6 term is HS18/FS19 Q4(iii)

blocks.html: Symmetries. $p^4$ is a scalar: $H'$ commutes with $\vec L$ and with parity, so the rotation symmetry and parity survive, $l$ and $m$ stay good quantum numbers. The hidden SO(4) symmetry (the Runge-Lenz vector, script 8.3) does not commute with $p^4$: expect the $l$-degeneracy at fixed $n$ to be lifted, while the $(2l+1)$-fold degeneracy in $m$ remains. The degenerate matrix is diagonal in $|n,l,m\rangle$ (see lesson 2), so $E^{(1)}_{nlm}=\langle nlm|H'|nlm\rangle$.

The trick (FS26 Q4(iii)). Do not compute $\langle p^4\rangle$ with derivatives. From $H_0|nlm\rangle=E_n|nlm\rangle$: $p^2|nlm\rangle=2m(E_n-V)|nlm\rangle=2m(E_n+e^2/r)|nlm\rangle$. Since $p^2$ is hermitian, $\langle p^4\rangle=\|p^2|nlm\rangle\|^2=4m^2\langle(E_n+e^2/r)^2\rangle$:

blocks.label: script (9.7.29) quotes the r^-3 analogue; a is the Bohr radius
with E_n = -mc^2 alpha^2/(2n^2), alpha = e^2/(hbar c)

blocks.html: Expectation values for $n=2$ from the given radial functions $R_{20}=\frac1{\sqrt{8a^3}}(2-\frac ra)e^{-r/2a}$, $R_{21}=\frac1{\sqrt{24a^3}}\frac rae^{-r/2a}$ with $\int_0^\infty r^ne^{-r/a}dr=a^{n+1}n!$: $\langle1/r\rangle=\frac1{4a}$ for both; $\langle1/r^2\rangle_{2,0}=\frac1{4a^2}$, $\langle1/r^2\rangle_{2,1}=\frac1{12a^2}$.

The shift is always negative (relativistic mass increase lowers the kinetic energy) and larger for small $l$: s-electrons come close to the nucleus, where $p^2$ is large. Sketch for (v): one $n$ level splits into $n$ sublevels labelled by $l$, $l=0$ lowest, each $(2l+1)$-fold degenerate, total shift negative with size $\sim\alpha^2|E_n|$.

Do not forget $E_n^2$ and the sign of $2e^2E_n\langle1/r\rangle$ ($E_n<0$). Another common error is using $\langle1/r^2\rangle=\langle1/r\rangle^2$. Also $\hbar^2/(ma)=e^2$, so convert $e^4/(a^2mc^2)=mc^2\alpha^4$ carefully.

options: the hidden SO(4) (Runge-Lenz): the $l$-degeneracy of fixed $n$ is lifted
check.explain: FS26 Q4(i): $l,m$ stay good, the accidental degeneracy is lost.

The relativistic correction of the $n=2$ levels is
options: negative for both $l=0$ and $l=1$, with $2s$ shifted more than $2p$ ($13/128$ versus $7/384$ in units of $mc^2\alpha^4$)

encounters.title: Time-dependent perturbation theory in one page

blocks.html: For $H=H_0+\lambda H'(t)$ the unperturbed propagator is $U_0(t,t_0)=e^{-iH_0(t-t_0)/\hbar}$, from $i\hbar\partial_tU_0=H_0U_0$ (HS21 Q4(i)). The perturbation is best treated in the Dirac (interaction) picture, $\Psi_D(t)=U_0^\dagger(t,t_0)\Psi(t)$, $U_D=U_0^\dagger U$:

First order: $U_D\approx1-\frac{i\lambda}\hbar\int_{t_0}^tH'_D$. Starting in $|i\rangle$ the amplitude for $|f\rangle\ne|i\rangle$ is $c_f=-\frac{i}{\hbar}\int dt'\,e^{i(E_f-E_i)t'/\hbar}\langle f|H'(t')|i\rangle$ and

The integral is a Fourier transform of the perturbation at the Bohr frequency $\omega_{fi}=(E_f-E_i)/\hbar$: a transition is only likely if $H'(t)$ contains that frequency. A constant $V$ switched on at $t_0=0$ gives $P=\frac{4|V|^2}{\Delta^2}\sin^2\frac{\Delta t}{2\hbar}$, $\Delta=E_f-E_i$: it oscillates with maximum $4|V|^2/\Delta^2$ for $\Delta\ne0$ (an off-resonant constant perturbation can only mix a little), and grows like $|V|^2t^2/\hbar^2$ for $\Delta\to0$.

The formula is first order: it needs $P\ll1$. For resonance ($\Delta\approx0$) it fails after $t\sim\hbar/|V|$; then Rabi oscillation between the two states, exactly like the exact two-level solution. The factor is $1/\hbar^2$ and the matrix element is $\langle f|H'|i\rangle$ in the Schroedinger picture.

check.explain: Matrix elements pick up the phase $e^{i(E_f-E_i)t/\hbar}$.

encounters.title: Non-degenerate perturbation theory to second order (FS19 Q4 (i))
encounters.goal: Derive $E^{(1)}_n$, $\psi^{(1)}_n$ and $E^{(2)}_n$ for $H=H_0+\lambda H'$ with non-degenerate $H_0$, using $\langle\psi_n|\psi^{(s)}\rangle=0$.
given: $H_0\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, $E_n\ne E_m$ for $n\neq m$, $\{\psi_m\}$ orthonormal and complete

steps.prompt: (a) Insert the ansatz and collect orders $\lambda^0,\lambda^1,\lambda^2$.
(b) Project the first-order equation on $\langle\psi_n|$.
steps.reveal: $\langle\psi_n|H_0=E_n\langle\psi_n|$ cancels $H_0\psi^{(1)}$ against $E_n\psi^{(1)}$. Left: $\langle n|H'|n\rangle=E^{(1)}\langle n|n\rangle$, so $E^{(1)}=\langle n|H'|n\rangle$.

steps.prompt: (c) Project the first-order equation on $\langle\psi_m|$, $m\ne n$, to get $\psi^{(1)}$.
steps.reveal: $(E_m-E_n)\langle m|\psi^{(1)}\rangle+\langle m|H'|n\rangle=0$ (using $\langle m|n\rangle=0$). Hence $\langle m|\psi^{(1)}\rangle=\frac{\langle m|H'|n\rangle}{E_n-E_m}$ and, with the convention $\langle n|\psi^{(1)}\rangle=0$, $\psi^{(1)}=\sum_{m\ne n}\frac{\langle m|H'|n\rangle}{E_n-E_m}\psi_m$.

steps.prompt: (d) Project the second-order equation on $\langle\psi_n|$.
steps.reveal: $\langle n|H'|\psi^{(1)}\rangle=E^{(1)}\langle n|\psi^{(1)}\rangle+E^{(2)}=E^{(2)}$ (convention). Insert $\psi^{(1)}$: $E^{(2)}=\sum_{m\ne n}\frac{\langle n|H'|m\rangle\langle m|H'|n\rangle}{E_n-E_m}=\sum_{m\neq n}\frac{|\langle m|H'|n\rangle|^2}{E_n-E_m}$.

steps.prompt: (e) When does the series make sense and what fails for degenerate levels?
steps.reveal: The coefficients $\frac{\langle m|\lambda H'|n\rangle}{E_n-E_m}$ must be small. If $E_m\to E_n$ the denominator vanishes: either $\langle m|H'|n\rangle=0$ (symmetry) or one must diagonalise $H'$ inside the degenerate subspace.

keyPoints: order-by-order equations with the same operator $H_0-E_n$
projection on $\langle\psi_n|$ kills the left side (hermiticity): gives $E^{(s)}$
projection on $\langle\psi_m|$ divides by $E_n-E_m$: gives the state

encounters.title: Degenerate first-order theory (FS22 Q4 (ii))
encounters.goal: For a three-fold degenerate level $E_m$ with orthonormal states $|\ell\rangle,|n\rangle,|k\rangle$ derive the equation for the first-order energy shifts.

steps.prompt: (a) Why must the zeroth-order state be written $\psi^{(0)}=c_\ell|\ell\rangle+c_n|n\rangle+c_k|k\rangle$ with unknown $c$?
steps.reveal: Every combination is an eigenstate of $H_0$ with energy $E_m$; the perturbation selects the right combination. The $\lambda^0$ equation does not fix the $c$'s.

steps.prompt: (b) Project the order-$\lambda$ equation on each degenerate state $\langle i|$.
steps.reveal: $\langle i|(H_0-E_m)=0$, so $0=\langle i|(E^{(1)}-H')|\psi^{(0)}\rangle$ for $i\in\{\ell,n,k\}$: $\sum_jH'_{ij}c_j=E^{(1)}c_i$.

steps.prompt: (c) State the resulting eigenvalue problem and its solution condition.
steps.reveal: $W c=E^{(1)}c$ with $W_{ij}=\langle i|H'|j\rangle$ a $3\times3$ hermitian matrix, solved by $\det(W-E^{(1)}\mathbb 1)=0$. The three eigenvalues are the first-order shifts, the eigenvectors the correct zeroth-order states.

steps.prompt: (d) Projection on states $\langle m'|$ outside the subspace.
steps.reveal: gives $\psi^{(1)}$ outside the subspace, as in the non-degenerate case, with $E_{m'}\neq E_m$ in the denominator. The components inside the subspace are fixed only at second order.

keyPoints: $\psi^{(0)}$ is a combination of all degenerate states
projection on the degenerate subspace gives $Wc=E^{(1)}c$

encounters.title: Relativistic correction $\langle p^4\rangle$ without derivatives (FS26 Q4 (iii))

steps.prompt: (a) Express $p^2|nlm\rangle$ through $E_n$ and $r$.
steps.reveal: $p^2=2m(H_0+e^2/r)$, so $p^2|nlm\rangle=2m(E_n+\frac{e^2}r)|nlm\rangle$.

steps.prompt: (b) Write $\langle p^4\rangle$ as a norm and insert (a).
steps.reveal: $\langle nlm|p^4|nlm\rangle=\langle p^2\psi|p^2\psi\rangle=4m^2\langle(E_n+e^2/r)^2\rangle$.

steps.prompt: (c) Expand the square and multiply with $-\frac1{8m^3c^2}$.
steps.reveal: $\langle p^4\rangle=4m^2(E_n^2+2e^2E_n\langle\frac1r\rangle+e^4\langle\frac1{r^2}\rangle)$, hence $E^{(1)}=-\frac{4m^2}{8m^3c^2}(\dots)=-\frac1{2mc^2}(\dots)$.

steps.prompt: (d) Insert $E_2=-\frac{e^2}{8a}$ and the $n=2$ expectation values.

encounters.title: Stark matrix element $\langle200|z|210\rangle=-3a_0$ (sheet 14 Q2)

source.where: Question 2 (hint with the n=2 wave functions)

encounters.goal: Compute the only non-zero element of $z$ in the $n=2$ subspace and the first-order energies in the field $\vec E=E\hat z$.

steps.prompt: (a) Which matrix elements of $z=r\cos\theta$ vanish by symmetry?
steps.reveal: $z$ is odd under parity, so only $l=0\leftrightarrow1$ couples, and $[L_z,z]=0$ forces $\Delta m=0$. In the $n=2$ subspace only $\langle200|z|210\rangle$ remains.

steps.prompt: (b) Separate the angular integral.
steps.reveal: $\int Y_{00}^*\cos\theta\,Y_{10}\,d\Omega=\frac{1}{\sqrt{4\pi}}\sqrt{\frac3{4\pi}}\,2\pi\int_{-1}^1u^2du=\frac1{\sqrt3}$.

steps.prompt: (c) Radial integral.
steps.reveal: With $R_{20}=\frac1{\sqrt2}a_0^{-3/2}(1-\frac r{2a_0})e^{-r/2a_0}$ and $R_{21}=\frac1{2\sqrt6}a_0^{-3/2}\frac r{a_0}e^{-r/2a_0}$: $\int_0^\infty R_{20}R_{21}r^3dr=\frac1{2\sqrt{12}}a_0^{-4}\int_0^\infty\big(1-\frac r{2a_0}\big)r^4e^{-r/a_0}dr$. Use $\int r^4e^{-r/a_0}=24a_0^5$ and $\frac1{2a_0}\int r^5e^{-r/a_0}=\frac{120a_0^6}{2a_0}=60a_0^5$: the bracket is $(24-60)a_0^5=-36a_0^5$, so the radial integral is $\frac{-36}{4\sqrt3}a_0=-3\sqrt3\,a_0$.

steps.prompt: (d) Combine and diagonalise.
steps.reveal: $\langle200|z|210\rangle=\frac1{\sqrt3}\cdot(-3\sqrt3\,a_0)=-3a_0$. $W=\begin{pmatrix}0&-\varepsilon\\-\varepsilon&0\end{pmatrix}$ with $\varepsilon=3|e|Ea_0$; eigenvalues $\pm3|e|Ea_0$ for $(|200\rangle\mp|210\rangle)/\sqrt2$; $|21\pm1\rangle$ stay at $E_2$.

encounters.title: First-order transition probability in the Dirac picture (HS21 Q4 (ii)-(iii))

steps.prompt: (a) Define $\Psi_D$ and $U_D$.
steps.reveal: $\Psi_D(t)=U_0^\dagger(t,t_0)\Psi(t)$, hence $U_D(t,t_0)=U_0^\dagger(t,t_0)\,U(t,t_0)$.

steps.prompt: (b) Differentiate $U_D$.
steps.reveal: $i\hbar\partial_tU_D=-U_0^\dagger H_0U+U_0^\dagger HU=U_0^\dagger\lambda H'U=\lambda H'_DU_D$ with $H'_D=U_0^\dagger H'U_0$ (use $i\hbar\partial_tU_0^\dagger=-U_0^\dagger H_0$).

steps.prompt: (c) Solve iteratively to first order.
steps.reveal: $U_D=1-\frac{i\lambda}\hbar\int_{t_0}^tH'_D(t')dt'+O(\lambda^2)$; the full solution is the time-ordered exponential.

steps.prompt: (d) Take the matrix element $\langle f|U_D|i\rangle$ for $f\ne i$ and square it.
steps.reveal: $\langle f|H'_D(t')|i\rangle=e^{i(E_f-E_i)t'/\hbar}\langle f|H'(t')|i\rangle$, so $c_f=-\frac{i}\hbar\int dt'e^{i\omega_{fi}t'}H'_{fi}(t')$ and $P_{i\to f}=|c_f|^2$.

keyPoints: first-order truncation of the Dyson series

encounters.title: Stark effect of the $n=2$ level (sheet 14 Q2)
encounters.problem: A hydrogen atom in the state manifold $n=2$ sits in a uniform field $\vec E=E\hat z$, $\Delta H=-eEz$ ($e<0$). Find the first-order energy shifts and the states, and the size of the shift for $E=10^6$ V/m. Source: sheet 14, Q2.
symbols: matrix of $\Delta H$ in the degenerate subspace

derivation.title: Method
derivation.html: Four states with the same $E_2$: degenerate PT. Selection rules ($z$ odd, $\Delta m=0$) leave one off-diagonal element $\langle200|z|210\rangle=-3a_0$. Diagonalise the $2\times2$ block.

steps.prompt: Which states are coupled by $\Delta H=-eEz$ inside $n=2$?
options: only $|200\rangle\leftrightarrow|210\rangle$: opposite parity and the same $m=0$

why.3: $\langle z\rangle$ in a definite-parity state vanishes, but not between different states in the degenerate subspace.

steps.prompt: Why can you use degenerate PT with the $2\times2$ block instead of the sum over $m\neq n$?
options: the denominators $E_2-E_2$ vanish; the first-order shifts are the eigenvalues of $W$ on the subspace

why.1: Smallness is not the issue; zero denominators are.
why.2: Odd parity explains the zero diagonal, not the use of degenerate theory.

items.why: Nothing to compute before the subspace is chosen.

items.text: Use $[L_z,\Delta H]=0$ and parity to find the non-zero elements of $W$
items.why: Selection rules reduce the labour before any integral.
Needs the matrix structure from above.

encounters.title: A linear perturbation of the oscillator: exact vs perturbation theory
encounters.problem: $H=\frac{p^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2x^2+Fx$. Compute the energy shifts to second order in $F$ using $x=x_0(a+a^\dagger)/\sqrt2$, $x_0=\sqrt{\hbar/m\omega}$, and compare with the exact result. Source: method of sheet 14 Q1 and HS25 Q3 (given formulas).

derivation.title: Method
derivation.html: $H'=Fx=\frac{Fx_0}{\sqrt2}(a+a^\dagger)$ couples only $n\to n\pm1$, so $E^{(1)}=0$ and the sum in $E^{(2)}$ has two terms.

steps.prompt: Which matrix elements of $H'$ appear in $E^{(2)}_n$?

why.0: That would be $x^2$; $x$ changes $n$ by one.
why.1: That is first order and vanishes for $x$ by parity.

steps.prompt: Type $|\langle n+1|H'|n\rangle|$ (symbols F, x0, n).
Type $E^{(2)}_n$ (symbols F, x0, hbar, omega).
Compare with the exact solution (complete the square).
options: the exact result has all orders in $F$
exact $E_n=\hbar\omega(n+\frac12)-\frac{F^2}{2m\omega^2}$: the series terminates at second order and the states are shifted Gaussians
the exact energy depends on $n$ through the shift

why.1: Completing the square subtracts a constant, so the level goes down.
why.3: The shift is a constant for all $n$.

steps.prompt: Bonus: with $g=Fx_0/\hbar\omega=0.3$, $E^{(2)}_n$ in units of $\hbar\omega$.

encounters.title: Time-dependent PT: a constant kick (HS21 Q4 (iii))
encounters.problem: At $t=0$ a constant coupling $V=\langle f|H'|i\rangle$ is switched on between two states with $E_f-E_i=\Delta\ne0$. Find the first-order probability $P_{i\to f}(t)$. Source: HS21 Q4, formula (20).
symbols: amplitude of $|f\rangle$ in the Dirac picture

derivation.title: Method
derivation.html: Insert the constant matrix element in the first-order formula and integrate the phase $e^{i\Delta t'/\hbar}$.

steps.prompt: Which expression is the first-order amplitude?

why.0: The Dirac-picture matrix element carries the phase $e^{i\Delta t'/\hbar}$.
why.2: That is the static (adiabatic) admixture, not the amplitude after a sudden switch-on.

steps.prompt: Type $|c_f|^2$ (symbols V, D, t, hbar).
What happens for $\Delta\to0$?
options: $P\to V^2t^2/\hbar^2$ grows quadratically until first-order theory breaks down at $t\sim\hbar/V$
$P$ stays bounded by $4V^2/\Delta^2$ which tends to infinity, so nothing special

why.2: The bound diverges but the limit is the quadratic growth; the expansion needs $P\ll1$.
why.3: The growth is quadratic, not instantaneous.

steps.prompt: Bonus: $V=0.01$, $\Delta=0.5$, $t=\pi$, $\hbar=1$ (energies in the same unit). Compute $P$.

encounters.title: Relativistic corrections of the oscillator (FS19 Q4 = HS18 Q4)

source.where: Question 4 [Time-independent perturbation theory, 21 pt] (German original: FS 19 Aufgabe 4)

encounters.instructions: Solve on paper under the timer (2 min per point). Enter the final numbers as coefficients of the expansion in $\epsilon=\hbar\omega/mc^2$.
statement: In this question we study time-independent non-degenerate perturbation theory.

(i) Let $H_0$ be a Hamiltonian whose complete set of eigenfunctions is described by $H_0\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, $n=0,1,2,\dots$, where $E_n\neq E_m$ for $n\ne m$. We want to find the eigenfunctions of the perturbed Hamiltonian $H=H_0+\lambda H'$. Make an ansatz for $\psi$ and $E$ as a power series in $\lambda$ and determine the equations order by order in $\lambda$ (up to $\lambda^2$). Explain how to find the perturbed eigenfunction $\psi$ to first order in $\lambda$ and the corresponding eigenvalue to second order in $\lambda$. (You should work with the convention that the higher order corrections to the eigenfunction are orthogonal to the leading term.) [10 pt]

(ii) Now consider the case where $H_0$ is the Hamiltonian of the harmonic oscillator $H=\frac{p^2}{2m}+\frac12m\omega^2x^2=\frac{\hbar\omega}{2}(aa^\dagger+a^\dagger a)$, where $x=\sqrt{\frac\hbar{2m\omega}}(a+a^\dagger)$, $p=-\sqrt{\frac{\hbar m\omega}2}\,i(a-a^\dagger)$. Work out the perturbed eigenvalues (up to second order) for the perturbation described by the first relativistic correction term $H'=\alpha p^4$, where $\alpha=-(8m^3c^2)^{-1}$, for the case where the unperturbed energy is $E_0=\frac12\hbar\omega$. [7 pt]

(iii) In order to calculate the full relativistic correction to order $mc^2(\hbar\omega/mc^2)^2$ we also need to include the second order relativistic correction term to the Hamiltonian, namely $H''=\beta p^6$, where $\beta=(16m^5c^4)^{-1}$. How does this correction affect the result you obtained in (ii)? [4 pt]

finalAnswers.prompt: (ii) First-order coefficient of $\epsilon\hbar\omega$ in $E_0$ ($\epsilon=\hbar\omega/mc^2$). Enter the absolute value.
(iii) Coefficient of $\epsilon^2\hbar\omega$ added by $\beta p^6$ at first order (sign: positive).

keyPoints: (i) ansatz, three order equations; $E^{(1)}=\langle n|H'|n\rangle$, $\psi^{(1)}=\sum\frac{H'_{mn}}{E_n-E_m}\psi_m$, $E^{(2)}=\sum\frac{|H'_{mn}|^2}{E_n-E_m}$ with the convention $\langle\psi_n|\psi^{(s)}\rangle=0$
(iii) $\langle0|p^6|0\rangle=15(m\hbar\omega/2)^3$ shifts the energy by $+\frac{15}{128}\epsilon^2\hbar\omega$: same order as $E^{(2)}$ of $H'$, so total $\frac{39}{512}\epsilon^2\hbar\omega$
Check: expanding the exact $\sqrt{p^2c^2+m^2c^4}$ to this order; the $p^6$ term is needed for consistency

encounters.title: Fine structure corrections of hydrogen (FS26 Q4)
encounters.instructions: Solve on paper under the timer. Enter the final numbers: expectation values in units of powers of $a$ and the energy shifts in units of $mc^2\alpha^4$ (absolute values).
statement: Typical speeds of the electron in the hydrogen atom are $v/c\approx0.007$, and thus relativistic corrections play a role. The relativistic kinetic energy is $T=\sqrt{p^2c^2+m^2c^4}-mc^2$.

(i) Expand $T$ to show that the first order relativistically corrected Hamiltonian of the hydrogen atom is $H=\frac{p^2}{2m}-\frac{p^4}{8m^3c^2}-\frac{e^2}{r}=H_0-\frac{p^4}{8m^3c^2}$. Which symmetries of the hydrogen atom are preserved and which do you expect to be broken when this correction is added? [4 points]

We want to find the energy corrections using perturbation theory. The bound eigenstates of $H_0$ are $|n,l,m\rangle$, $n=1,2,3,\dots$, $l=0,\dots,n-1$, $m=-l,\dots,l$. States with the same quantum number $n$ are degenerate, $H_0|n,l,m\rangle=E_n|n,l,m\rangle$.

(ii) In degenerate perturbation theory the first order energy corrections to $E_n$ are the eigenvalues of the matrix $(\langle n,l',m'|H'|n,l,m\rangle)_{l,m;l',m'}$, where $H'$ is the perturbation. Use the symmetries of the Hamiltonian from (i) to show that the first order correction $E^{(1)}_{n,l,m}$ of the state $|n,l,m\rangle$ is simply given by $E^{(1)}_{n,l,m}=\langle n,l,m|H'|n,l,m\rangle$, where $H'=-\frac{p^4}{8m^3c^2}$. [4 points]

(iii) Show that $E^{(1)}_{n,l,m}=-\frac1{2mc^2}\Big(E_n^2+2e^2E_n\big\langle\frac1r\big\rangle_{n,l,m}+e^4\big\langle\frac1{r^2}\big\rangle_{n,l,m}\Big)$ where $\langle O\rangle_{n,l,m}:=\langle n,l,m|O|n,l,m\rangle$. Hint: Find an expression for $p^2|n,l,m\rangle$ in terms of $E_n$ and $V$, and use this to find an expression for the expectation value of $p^4$. [4 points]

(iv) For the $n=2$ wavefunctions $\psi_{2,l,m}(r,\theta,\phi)=R_{2,l}(r)Y_{l,m}(\theta,\phi)$, calculate $\langle\frac1r\rangle_{2,l,m}$ and $\langle\frac1{r^2}\rangle_{2,l,m}$ using $\langle r^\alpha\rangle_{2,l,m}=\int_0^\infty dr\,r^2\,r^\alpha(R_{2,l}(r))^2$. Hints: $R_{2,0}(r)=\frac1{\sqrt{8a^3}}\big(2-\frac ra\big)e^{-r/2a}$, $R_{2,1}(r)=\frac1{\sqrt{24a^3}}\frac rae^{-r/2a}$, where $a$ is the Bohr radius; and $\int_0^\infty dr\,r^ne^{-r/a}=a^{n+1}n!$. [6 points]

(v) Sketch the splitting of the $n$-th energy level due to the relativistic correction to the kinetic energy, depending on the quantum numbers $l,m$. Hint: What can you say about the sign of the energy correction? Furthermore, what is the qualitative $l$ dependence of $\langle\frac1r\rangle$ and $\langle\frac1{r^2}\rangle$ (using (iv))? Note that the wavefunction of $|n,l,m\rangle$ scales as $r^l$ for $r\to0$. [3 points]

finalAnswers.prompt: $|E^{(1)}_{2,0,0}|$ in units of $mc^2\alpha^4$ (the shift is negative).

keyPoints: (i) $T=\frac{p^2}{2m}-\frac{p^4}{8m^3c^2}+\dots$; rotation (all $\vec L$) and parity preserved, the hidden SO(4) (Runge-Lenz) broken, so $l$-degeneracy lifted
(ii) $H'$ commutes with $L^2,L_z$, so it does not connect different $(l,m)$: matrix diagonal

encounters.title: Degenerate perturbation theory with a rotation term (FS22 Q4)
encounters.instructions: Solve on paper under the timer. Enter the coefficients of $\lambda\hbar\omega$ and the degeneracy.
statement: Let $H_0$ be a Hamiltonian whose complete set of eigenfunctions is described by $H_0\psi_n=E_n\psi_n$, $n=0,1,2,\dots$. We want to find the eigenfunctions of the perturbed Hamiltonian $H=H_0+\lambda H'$.

(i) Let $\psi$ be an eigenstate of the perturbed system with energy $E$. Make an ansatz for $\psi$ and $E$ as a power series in $\lambda$, and derive the equations for the perturbation at any order $\lambda^s$. [5 pt] [Hint: Derive a general equation that holds for $s\ge2$, and then treat the cases $s=0$ and $s=1$ separately.]

(ii) Let us assume that the unperturbed energy $E_m$ of the solution whose perturbed energy we want to determine is 3-fold degenerate, and denote the corresponding orthonormal eigenstates of $H_0$ by $|\ell\rangle$, $|n\rangle$ and $|k\rangle$. Using the relevant relation from (i), derive an eigenvalue equation that determines the values of the perturbed energy $E$ of $H$ to first order in $\lambda$. (You do not need to solve this eigenvalue equation.) [4 pt]

(iii) Consider the three-dimensional harmonic oscillator $H_0=\hbar\omega\big(a^\dagger a+b^\dagger b+c^\dagger c+\frac32\big)$, where $(a,a^\dagger)$, $(b,b^\dagger)$ and $(c,c^\dagger)$ are the annihilation and creation operators associated to the three coordinate axes $x,y,z$, i.e. $x=\sqrt{\frac\hbar{2m\omega}}(a+a^\dagger)$, $p_x=-\sqrt{\frac{\hbar m\omega}2}\,i(a-a^\dagger)$, and similarly for $(y,p_y)$ and $(z,p_z)$. We take $H'$ to be the operator $H'=\omega L_z=\omega(xp_y-yp_x)$. Consider the three-fold degenerate eigenstates of $H_0$ with eigenvalue $E_m=\frac52\hbar\omega$, and determine the eigenvalues of the perturbed problem to first order in perturbation theory. [5 pt] [Hint: label the states $|n_a,n_b,n_c\rangle$; $a|1,n_b,n_c\rangle=|0,n_b,n_c\rangle$, $a|0,n_b,n_c\rangle=0$, $a^\dagger|0,n_b,n_c\rangle=|1,n_b,n_c\rangle$ and similarly for the other generators.]
(iv) Comment briefly on why you could have expected this result based on the representation theory of SO(3). [1 pt]

finalAnswers.prompt: (iii) The largest first-order shift in units of $\lambda\hbar\omega$.
(iii) The most negative first-order shift in units of $\lambda\hbar\omega$ (enter the signed value).
Unperturbed energy of the level in units of $\hbar\omega$.

keyPoints: (i) order $\lambda^s$ ($s\ge2$): $(H_0-E_m)\psi^{(s)}=\sum_{k\ge1}(E^{(k)}-\delta_{k1}H')\psi^{(s-k)}$ with $\psi^{(0)}$ in the degenerate subspace
(ii) project on $\langle\ell|,\langle n|,\langle k|$: $\det\big(\langle i|H'|j\rangle-E^{(1)}\delta_{ij}\big)=0$, $3\times3$ matrix
(iv) the level $\frac52\hbar\omega$ is the $l=1$ representation of SO(3) (vector $x,y,z$): $H'\propto L_z$ splits it into $m=1,0,-1$
